hook_text: The lion never eats grass. So why would lions starve if all the grass disappeared?
clip_script: Kruger National Park. The Sun shines on the grass. The grass makes food. A zebra eats the grass. A lion eats the zebra. Sun, grass, zebra, lion. That is a food chain, and the arrows show the energy moving along: from the food to the eater. Now a drought. The grass dies. The zebra go hungry. And the lion? She never eats grass, but she goes hungry too. Every link in the chain matters.
visual_style: Whiteboard Sun, grass, zebra and lion linked by arrows that light up one after another as energy moves along the chain.
mood: Exciting, like a game drive with a twist at the end.
pacing: Build one food chain link by link, then two more, then pull out a link to see what happens.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw a food chain with yourself at the end.
